subject: Computational complexity of computing inverse of sparse precision matrix

messages.author: b7028bcb2bc39c54
messages.subject: Computational complexity of computing inverse of sparse precision matrix
parts:
Hi All,

I am wondering the computational complexity of computing inverse of sparse precision matrix.

In my example, the mesh includes around 9000 vertices and I calculated the precision matrix Q on this mesh.

The problem occurs when I compute the inverse of Q. If I am using inla.qinv(), then it takes approximately 1 second. But if I am using ginv(), it takes approximately 1 hour.

I briefly know that inla.qinv() only compute the dominant elements in the Q matrix.

Can you tell me the computational complexity of this function?

Thanks and Regards,
Linh

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Computational complexity of computing inverse of sparse precision matrix
parts:
Hi Linh,
inla.qinv only computes the elements of the inverse that correspond to the non-zero elements of Q. This is enough to compute the score function (which only uses these elements) but not anything like computing this full inverse. 

If I remember correctly, the complexity once a cholesky factorisation has been computed is something like n log n. 

Details are in this paper. http://www.math.ntnu.no/~hrue/reports/S1-2005.pdf

And also in the original inla paper

Best wishes

Dan
